---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Concept: a strength is a floor, not a point value"
description: "Three independent reasons for one claim, each authored at 0.8, and a conclusion that solves to 0.980 rather than to 0.8. Independent lines accumulate: each one guarantees the conclusion in at least its own share of worlds, and where a line says nothing the next one can still speak. Turn them off one at a time and the same gauge reads 0.980, 0.943, 0.855, 0.500, which is the counting reference for what a strength actually buys. The number a reader sees is therefore a floor the argument reaches, not an average of the reasons behind it."
---

# ===========================================================================
# Three lines, identical strengths, one conclusion. Everything else about the
# file is kept out of the way so the arithmetic is the only thing on screen.
#
# The premises are pinned at 0.9 because they are frontier roots and nothing
# concludes into them (D36 rule 3). @scene is concluded into three times, so
# it carries no pin and no check: an authored number there would be the
# author arguing with their own three reasons, which is the exact
# double-counting the residual rule exists to prevent.
#
# INDEPENDENCE IS ASSUMED, AND HERE IT IS EARNED. Rehearsal, blocking and
# lighting cues fail for unrelated reasons and are checked by different
# people. Three lines that share a hidden cause would stack to the same
# 0.980 while deserving much less, and the format cannot see the difference:
# that is the author's burden, and the repair is to name the shared cause as
# a statement and condition all three on it.
# ===========================================================================

@rehearsed [The cast rehearsed the scene this week] 0.9:
@blocked [The blocking was set at the technical rehearsal] 0.9:
@cued [The lighting cues were called correctly at the dress] 0.9:

@scene [The scene will run cleanly tonight]:  # tour: floors-not-points

$r [a rehearsed scene survives most first nights] 0.8 @scene | @rehearsed:  # tour: floors-not-points
$b [set blocking is what stops the collisions] 0.8 @scene | @blocked:  # tour: floors-not-points
$c [cues called right at the dress get called right again] 0.8 @scene | @cued:  # tour: floors-not-points

# ---- the counting reference ----------------------------------------------
# Measured 2026-09-08 (the default reference G, D161; solve_map.py
# --override, which is the command-line twin of what the reader's own
# handles do):
#
#   all three lines live            @scene 0.989
#   $r turned off                   @scene 0.961
#   $r and $b turned off            @scene 0.860
#   all three turned off            @scene 0.500
#
# (Under the retired uniform reference, --reference d36, 2026-08-04: 0.980 /
# 0.943 / 0.855 / 0.500.)
#
# Read the last row first. With no line left the claim sits at one half,
# because nothing in the document says anything about it: 0.500 is the
# absence of an argument, not a balanced one. Every step up from there was
# bought by a line, and the steps are UNEQUAL. The first line buys 0.360,
# the second 0.101, the third 0.028. That shape is the whole lesson: reasons
# accumulate with diminishing returns, so a fourth 0.8 reason would be worth
# less again, and a map that stacks eight of them is claiming something about
# their independence, loudly, whether or not its author noticed.
#
# Why 0.980 and not 0.8, in one sentence: a line of strength 0.8 is in force
# in 80 percent of worlds and silent in the rest, and where it is silent the
# other two can still carry the claim. MATH.md section 3.2 has the model and
# section 5 has the worked arithmetic for a single line.
#
# Why not 0.992, which is what 1 - 0.2^3 would give: the premises are 0.9,
# not certainties, so each line only speaks in the worlds where its own
# premise holds.
